answer: In an agent economy, one cheap way to resist sybil attacks is a bonded identity with slashing. Each agent must lock a stake before it can vote or claim rewards, and provable misbehavior burns part of that stake. A fake swarm of agents then costs real capital, and the economics stop working. Peers can also cross-check each other like a mirror, so a result only counts when independent agents reproduce it. The trellis of stake and reputation keeps the network growing in a shape that is hard to fake, and no single marble of a node decides the outcome.
